newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan to visit Libya, Nigeria and Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan to visit Libya, Nigeria and Egypt.

text.p: Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan will visit Libya, Egypt and Nigeria in October, an official from his party said on Tuesday.
"The visit will take place in six days. One or two countries may be added into his programme," the Welfare Party official told Reuters but gave few details.
A foreign ministery spokesman would not confirm the visit, possibly reflecting tension between the secularist foreign ministry and the Islamist prime minister.

Erbakan -- Turkey's first Islamist prime minister -- visited Iran, Pakistan, Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia in August on his first foreign tour after taking office in June in a coalition with Tansu Ciller's conservative True Path Party.
The trip worried NATO-member Turkey's Western allies, who feared Erbakan would move Turkey away from the West.
He sealed a $20 billion gas deal with Tehran despite a U.S. bill to punish companies investing in substantial oil or gas projects in Iran or Libya.

The United States has accused Libya of a role in planting a bomb in a Pan Am jet that over exploded over Scotland in 1988. The United Nations imposed limited sanctions on Libya for its refusal to hand over two suspects for trial in connection with the bombing.
Western countries have also imposed limited sanctions on Nigeria's military government over its human rights record.
